chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who raised it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Nothing spoils the water except that which has flowing blood."

key_terms.سَائِلَةٌ: flowing, meaning blood that flows when the body is cut
key_terms.نَفْسٌ: a living soul, here referring to an animal life
key_terms.يُفْسِدُ: renders corrupt or impure in legal context
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءَ: water used in rulings of taharah and impurity

ai.seo_question: What kinds of dead creatures make water impure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and water. It states that water is not corrupted except by a creature that possesses flowing blood, making it significant in fiqh discussions of najasah and taharah.
